mcqs.question: Which of the following comparisons correctly identifies the organism that is a protozoan?

options.A: Amoeba proteus – a multicellular fungus; Paramecium caudatum – a unicellular protozoan.
options.B: Paramecium caudatum – a unicellular protozoan; Saccharomyces cerevisiae – a unicellular fungus.
options.C: Euglena gracilis – a multicellular algae; Plasmodium falciparum – a unicellular bacterium.
options.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae – a unicellular protozoan; Candida albicans – a multicellular algae.

mcqs.answer: Paramecium caudatum – a unicellular protozoan; Saccharomyces cerevisiae – a unicellular fungus.
mcqs.explanation: Option B correctly pairs Paramecium caudatum, which is a well‑known protozoan, with a fungus. The other options either misclassify the organisms or assign the wrong kingdom, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a microscopic alga commonly studied in freshwater ecosystems?
mcqs.explanation: Chlorella vulgaris is a unicellular green alga that is microscopic and lives in freshwater. Penicillium is a fungus, Amoeba is a protozoan, and Streptococcus is a bacterium, so they are not algae.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that microorganisms have diverse roles
mcqs.question: Which statement best illustrates the diverse roles played by microorganisms?

options.A: All microorganisms cause diseases in humans.
options.B: Microorganisms only decompose dead organic matter.
options.C: Microorganisms can decompose waste, fix atmospheric nitrogen, and cause infections.
options.D: Microorganisms are only useful in food fermentation.

mcqs.answer: Microorganisms can decompose waste, fix atmospheric nitrogen, and cause infections.
mcqs.explanation: Option C captures the wide range of functions: decomposition, nitrogen fixation (beneficial), and disease causation (harmful). Options A, B, and D are too narrow, ignoring many other roles.

mcqs.question: Which of the following lists includes the four major groups of microorganisms studied in Class 8 science?
mcqs.explanation: The curriculum groups microorganisms into bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and algae. Viruses, insects, plants, and archaea are not part of the four groups emphasized at this level.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise differences in their structures and habitats
mcqs.question: Which pair correctly matches a type of microorganism with its typical structure and habitat?

options.A: Bacteria – multicellular; found in dry deserts
options.B: Fungi – multicellular filaments; thrive in moist, decaying organic matter
options.C: Protozoa – cell walls made of cellulose; live in acidic hot springs
options.D: Algae – lack chlorophyll; inhabit sterile laboratory media

mcqs.answer: Fungi – multicellular filaments; thrive in moist, decaying organic matter
mcqs.explanation: Fungi are composed of filamentous hyphae (multicellular) and are commonly found in moist, nutrient‑rich environments. The other options contain inaccurate structural or habitat details.

mcqs.question: Which of the following organisms is a bacterium that commonly inhabits the human gut?
mcqs.explanation: Escherichia coli is a gram‑negative bacterium that lives in the intestines of humans and many animals. Saccharomyces is a yeast (fungus), Paramecium is a protozoan, and Chlorella is an alga.

mcqs.question: Which organism below is an example of a fungus used in antibiotic production?
mcqs.explanation: Penicillium chrysogenum produces the antibiotic penicillin. Streptococcus is a bacterium, Euglena is a protist/alga, and Amoeba is a protozoan, so they are not fungi.

mcqs.question: A student observes a single‑celled organism moving by extending and retracting pseudopodia in a drop of pond water. Which organism is the student most likely observing?
mcqs.explanation: Amoeba proteus moves using pseudopodia, a hallmark of many protozoa. Chlorella is an alga, Streptococcus is a bacterium, and Penicillium is a fungus, none of which exhibit pseudopodial movement.
